text.arabic_uthmani: لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلَٰثَةٍۢ ۘ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّآ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۚ وَإِن لَّمْ يَنتَهُوا۟ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

words.gloss_range: oath particle prefixed to the verification particle; launches the verse as sworn certainty rather than neutral report
words.prose: {{ar:لَّ}} ({{tr:la}}) fuses the oath opening with the following verification particle, so the ayah begins as a sworn verdict before the quoted claim is even heard. It also sets the outer divine emphatic verdict against the inner human emphatic claim, joins the same surah-internal Christological adjudication sequence already heard at 5:17 and 5:72, and foreshadows the emphatic threat near the close.

topics.headline: sworn verdict launch
topics.summary: The reader notices that the ayah begins with judicial certainty, not neutral reportage.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins with oath-strength certainty and places that outer emphasis over against the quoted human assertion.
topics.reason: The oath particle is licensed by QAC as an oath opening before the verification particle, and the CRITICAL rows coherently tie that opening to verdict-first architecture and same-surah echo.

words.gloss_range: verification particle before a perfect verb; confirms the completed reality of the verdict
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) makes the following perfect verdict grammatically verified as already realized. The reader should hear the condemnation as established before the speech content is quoted.

topics.headline: verified completed verdict
topics.summary: The reader notices that the disbelief verdict is presented as settled before the quote unfolds.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disbelief verdict is presented as settled before the quote unfolds.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as verification before the perfect verb, matching the CRITICAL claim.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect verdict verb; locally absolute and intransitive, naming culpable denial generated by the utterance
words.root_gloss_range: broad root field includes covering, denial, rejection, and ingratitude; local usage selects culpable denial while preserving covering pressure
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرَ}} ({{tr:kafara}}) is a Form I perfect verdict: the act is stated before the plural subject is unpacked, and the verb is left without an object, so the utterance itself creates the state of covering-denial. The root {{ar:ك ف ر}} ({{tr:k-f-r}}) returns near the punishment clause, binding speech, deity language, tactile contact, and pain into one chain from utterance to verdict to consequence; the opening formula also pairs with the denunciation at 5:17.

topics.headline: absolute covering-denial verdict
topics.summary: The reader notices that the statement is judged as culpable denial before any neutral paraphrase can take over.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the statement is judged as culpable denial before any neutral paraphrase can take over.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I intransitive parse supports the verdict force, while lexical rows preserve covering-denial pressure without activating unrelated branches.

topics.headline: opening and closing verdict frame
topics.summary: The reader notices that the same root binds the initial accusation to the threatened group near the end.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same root binds the initial accusation to the threatened group near the end while the surrounding vocabulary links speech, deity language, contact, and pain.
topics.reason: The later plural verb in the punishment clause provides the concrete return of the same root.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun functioning as subject of the verdict and introducing the speech-defined group
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not leave the accusation vague: it supplies the subject of the verdict and immediately defines that group by the following speech act. The same relative frame later reappears in the punishment object phrase, keeping verdict and consequence attached to the same speech-defined class, while the opening pattern also belongs with the parallel denunciations at 5:17 and 5:72.

topics.headline: speech-defined subject
topics.summary: The reader notices that the condemned group is identified by what they say, not by an undefined label.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condemned group is identified by what they say, not by an undefined label.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the relative pronoun the subject of the opening verdict with the following saying clause as its identifier.

topics.headline: relative frame echo
topics.summary: The reader notices that the opening group frame returns in the threat, binding accusation and consequence.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening group frame returns in the threat and also participates in the repeated 5:17, 5:72, and 5:73 denunciation pattern.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL echo rows are coherent with the second relative pronoun in the apodosis.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect speech verb introducing a complete quoted proposition
words.root_gloss_range: root field centers on saying and articulated speech; local usage selects doctrinal utterance as the culpable act
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) introduces a full quoted proposition, so the condemned material is the doctrinal claim as speech, not one isolated word. The perfect report is later answered by an imperfect speech verb, turning a past utterance into an ongoing condition to abandon; it enacts the kind of triadic saying forbidden by the "do not say three" command at 4:171 and stands alongside the parallel claim formulas at 5:17 and 5:72.

topics.headline: quoted doctrinal speech
topics.summary: The reader notices that the offense is a proposition uttered as doctrine.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense is a proposition uttered as doctrine.
topics.reason: The verb governs a quotation block, and the speech-root rows correctly treat the utterance as doctrinal content.

topics.headline: past speech becomes ongoing liability
topics.summary: The reader notices that the ayah pairs the completed report with later ongoing saying as the thing to stop.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah pairs the completed report with later ongoing saying as the thing to stop.
topics.reason: The later imperfect speech verb supplies the local anchor for the aspect shift.

topics.headline: anti-triadic speech field
topics.summary: The reader notices that this saying participates in the Quranic correction of triadic speech (4:171).
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this saying enacts the triadic speech forbidden at 4:171 and belongs with the repeated claim formulas at 5:17 and 5:72.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references, especially 4:171 and 5:17, and the local quote is the same doctrinal field.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle inside the quoted speech; governs the inner nominal predication
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) marks that the speakers assert their own claim emphatically inside the quotation, governs the divine name as the subject of that inner clause, and sets up the ordinal predicate as the core error. The ayah therefore stages a clash of emphases: the outer sworn verdict condemns what the inner emphatic speech tries to establish.

topics.headline: inner emphatic claim
topics.summary: The reader notices that the quoted claim is asserted with its own emphasis, not reported as a loose slogan.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted claim is a controlled inner predication, with its own emphasis, subject, and ordinal predicate.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as governing the quoted nominal clause, and the CRITICAL rows correctly read it as inner assertion.

topics.headline: outer and inner emphasis
topics.summary: The reader notices the rhetorical contest between divine verdict emphasis and human claim emphasis.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rhetorical contest between divine verdict emphasis and human claim emphasis.
topics.reason: The opening emphatic frame and the inner particle are both locally present.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as the accusative subject of the quoted predication
words.root_gloss_range: root field links divine name and deity language; local word remains a proper noun while the following correction broadens to deity category
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) is the named subject inside the condemned predication, so the claim is directly about Allah rather than a generic divine category. The correction then moves from this proper name to the common deity noun, letting worship, refuge, and bewilderment associations remain controlled background while denying every rival object of worship or refuge and affirming only one.

topics.headline: proper name inside the claim
topics.summary: The reader notices that the offense predicates the triadic role directly of Allah.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense predicates the triadic role directly of Allah.

topics.headline: proper name to deity category
topics.summary: The reader notices that the refutation broadens from the named Allah to the whole deity category.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refutation broadens from the named Allah to the whole deity category.
topics.reason: The later common deity nouns provide the local basis for the name-category contrast.

words.gloss_range: ordinal numeral as predicate and construct head; places the referent as member-position within a counted three
words.root_gloss_range: number root field centers on threeness; local phrase selects ordinal thirdness linked to a genitive counted set
words.prose: {{ar:ثَالِثُ}} ({{tr:thālithu}}) is the predicate of the quoted clause and the construct head of the following cardinal, making the claim tighter than a free slogan about three. It assigns a member-position within a counted set, which the later oneness adjective directly overturns; the ayah reports as a genitive predicate formula the triadic speech warned against by "do not say three" at 4:171.

topics.headline: ordinal construct predicate
topics.summary: The reader notices that the claim grammatically positions Allah as a member within a counted triad.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim grammatically positions Allah as a member within a counted triad.
topics.reason: The ordinal is the predicate and construct head, so the CRITICAL rows about relational thirdness are locally licensed.

topics.headline: three-one antithesis
topics.summary: The reader notices that the verse builds its central refutation as a number conflict: third-of-three against one.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse builds its central refutation as a number conflict: third-of-three against one.
topics.reason: The following oneness word and the 4:171 reference make the numerical opposition explicit.

words.gloss_range: indefinite cardinal in genitive construct relation; supplies the counted set for the ordinal
words.root_gloss_range: number root field centers on threeness; local usage selects an indefinite three-set rather than a named list
words.prose: {{ar:ثَلَٰثَةٍۢ}} ({{tr:thalāthatin}}) supplies the counted set governed by the ordinal and leaves that set indefinite. The payoff is that the ayah condemns the triadic configuration as such, without needing to name the members; its genitive form also contrasts with the nominative anti-triadic wording at 4:171.

topics.headline: indefinite three-set
topics.summary: The reader notices that the claim targets a counted three-configuration, not only a named list of members.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim targets a counted three-configuration, not only a named list of members.
topics.reason: The word is a genitive indefinite cardinal under construct governance, supporting the rows about unspecified counted configuration.

topics.headline: quote closes before refutation
topics.summary: The reader notices that the nasalized indefinite ending helps mark the close of the condemned quote before the corrective clause begins.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the nasalized indefinite ending helps mark the close of the condemned quote before the corrective clause begins.
topics.reason: The clause boundary after the quoted phrase licenses the structural hinge rows.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the corrective assertion after the quote
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge from human assertion to divine correction. Everything before it is the condemned quotation; everything after it begins the monotheistic answer.

topics.headline: correction hinge
topics.summary: The reader notices the exact turn from quoted error to corrective truth.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact turn from quoted error to corrective truth.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify this conjunction as resumptive at the quote-to-correction transition.

words.gloss_range: negative particle beginning the strengthened negation-exception formula
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the corrective formula by beginning a categorical negation that will not stop at denial; it is designed to pass through exception into exclusive affirmation. The refutation therefore negates the whole deity class before affirming only one.

topics.headline: categorical negation to exception
topics.summary: The reader notices that the correction works by exhaustive denial followed by exclusive affirmation.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the correction works by exhaustive denial followed by exclusive affirmation.
topics.reason: The particle is locally part of the reinforced negation-exception construction, matching the CRITICAL rows.

words.gloss_range: emphatic preposition inside the negative construction; widens negation over the class
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) strengthens the negation rather than marking ordinary source. Its payoff is exhaustive scope: the clause denies any deity-instance before the exception is allowed.

topics.headline: exhaustive negation scope
topics.summary: The reader notices that the negation leaves no secondary divine member available before the exception.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation leaves no secondary divine member available before the exception.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as emphatic within the negative construction, so the exhaustive-scope rows are locally supported.

words.gloss_range: common deity noun under emphatic negation; indefinite genitive gives class-wide force
words.root_gloss_range: root field includes worship, refuge, and deity language; local usage selects common deity category under total negation
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَٰهٍ}} ({{tr:ilāhin}}) is the deity category under exhaustive negation: not one possible object of worship or refuge is left standing. Its repetition after the exception makes the formula precise: the same category is first denied as a class and then affirmed only as one.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refutation denies every possible deity category before the exception.
topics.reason: The indefinite genitive under emphatic negation supports class-wide denial.

topics.summary: The reader notices that the same deity noun moves from negated class to sole affirmed instance.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same deity noun moves from negated class to sole affirmed instance.
topics.reason: The later nominative deity noun provides the local echo.

words.gloss_range: exception particle pivoting total negation into restriction
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) is the pivot of the monotheistic formula: the prior total negation exists to arrive at a single permitted exception. The word turns denial into restriction rather than leaving the clause as bare negation.

topics.headline: exception pivot
topics.summary: The reader notices that exclusivity is built into the syntax, not added as commentary.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exclusivity is built into the syntax, not added as commentary.

words.gloss_range: affirmed common deity noun after exception; nominative and qualified by oneness
words.root_gloss_range: root field includes deity, worship, and refuge language; local usage selects the sole affirmed deity category
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَٰهٌۭ}} ({{tr:ilāhun}}) is the same deity category now standing after the exception as the sole affirmed instance. Its nominative position and following adjective make the correction positive and restrictive: deity is affirmed only as one, not as a member within a triad.

topics.headline: sole affirmed deity
topics.summary: The reader notices that the formula does not deny divinity absolutely; it affirms only the one deity after restriction.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the formula does not deny divinity absolutely; it affirms only the one deity after restriction.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated deity noun carries the logic from denial into exclusive affirmation.
topics.reason: The earlier genitive deity noun and this nominative noun create the exact local echo.

words.gloss_range: numeral adjective qualifying the affirmed deity; countable one directly answers the counted three
words.root_gloss_range: root field centers on oneness and unity; local usage selects numerical singularity in direct contrast to threeness
words.prose: {{ar:وَٰحِدٌۭ}} ({{tr:wāḥidun}}) grammatically qualifies the affirmed deity, so oneness is attached to the noun rather than floating as an aside. Its numerical force is tuned to answer the preceding three-field as countable singularity rather than only abstract uniqueness, and the same monotheistic formula appears in the anti-triadic correction at 4:171 before the verse turns to consequence.

topics.headline: one answers three
topics.summary: The reader notices that numerical oneness directly counters the third-of-three claim.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that numerical oneness directly counters the third-of-three claim.

topics.summary: The reader notices that the doctrinal correction is completed before the conditional threat begins.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the doctrinal correction is completed before the conditional threat begins.

words.gloss_range: second resumptive conjunction moving from correction to conditional warning
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the third movement of the ayah: verdict, correction, then conditional warning. The hinge matters because the threat follows a completed monotheistic correction and still leaves room for desistance.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah turning from doctrine into consequence without losing the possibility of return.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle introducing possible non-desistance and its consequence
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) makes the threat conditional rather than fatalistic: if they do not desist, the consequence follows. The word opens a mercy window after a severe verdict, holding possible escape and emphatic warning together.

topics.headline: conditional mercy window
topics.summary: The reader notices that the ayah gives a path of desistance after the verdict.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah gives a path of desistance after the verdict.

words.gloss_range: negative jussive particle making non-desistance the condition
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) negates the required act of stopping and governs the following jussive verb. The warning is therefore triggered by failure to cease the ongoing speech, not by an unspecified failure detached from the claim.

topics.headline: negative desistance condition
topics.summary: The reader notices that the threatened consequence depends specifically on not stopping.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the threatened consequence depends specifically on not stopping.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII jussive desistance verb; demands self-stopping from the stated speech
words.root_gloss_range: root field includes ending, forbidding, and desisting; local Form VIII selects self-involved cessation under conditional pressure
words.prose: {{ar:يَنتَهُوا۟}} ({{tr:yantahū}}) is the demanded stopping-point: the speakers must bring their own utterance to an end. Form VIII gives the desistance an inward, self-prohibiting force, and 4:171 supplies the direct imperative counterpart to this conditional warning.

topics.headline: self-desistance from speech
topics.summary: The reader notices that the demanded remedy is active self-cessation, not merely a change of tone.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the demanded remedy is active self-cessation, not merely a change of tone.

words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:yaqūlūna}}) closes the condition by naming the ongoing speech they must stop. It echoes the earlier perfect speech verb: what was once reported as a completed claim is now treated as present persistence and the object of required desistance.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the issue is continued saying, not only a past statement.

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) opens the apodosis with assertion, and the following heavy emphasis on the verb completes the warning complex. The conditional path is real, but if non-desistance continues, the consequence is presented as certain.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consequence is not tentative once the condition is met.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ثَالِثُ ثَلَاثَةٍ is directly corrected by إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ordinal image makes Allah a member who completes a counted set, while the unity branch denies partner, partition, and multiplication. The correction therefore rejects divine componenthood, not merely an incorrect total.

activation_trace.role: The third-as-completer image supplies the positional mechanism of adding one member to two.
Unity without partner, division, or multiplication supplies the direct negation of membered deity.
The worshipped-deity image fixes the disputed count to the category of worship, rather than to three unrelated entities.

changed_reading.before: The ayah simply replaces the number three with the number one.
changed_reading.after: The ayah rejects placing Allah as a member or part inside any counted divine composite; the one deity is without partner or partition.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: قَالُوا and يَقُولُونَ frame the proposition, while كَفَرَ and كَفَرُوا repeat the diagnosis.
baseline_models.mechanism: The saying branch can denote an adopted doctrine, and the disbelief branch can denote covering truth. Repetition turns a single utterance into a maintained verbal creed whose continued circulation performs the covering.

activation_trace.role: Saying as belief or school supplies the durable doctrinal stance behind both the initial and continuing speech.
Covering the truth supplies the functional effect assigned to the maintained proposition.
Cessation supplies a possible break in the mechanism, showing that persistence rather than bare historical utterance is at issue.

changed_reading.before: The ayah reports and condemns one erroneous sentence.
changed_reading.after: The ayah diagnoses a repeatedly maintained creed that covers unitary worship, while making cessation from that verbal practice a live possibility.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional لَمْ يَنتَهُوا is followed by the emphatic لَيَمَسَّنَّ.
baseline_models.mechanism: One branch marks an endpoint at which motion stops; the other marks an effect reaching and touching its object. The warning creates a threshold: end the saying before its consequence crosses into felt contact.

activation_trace.role: The reached endpoint supplies the stopping threshold offered by the conditional.
An effect reaching a person supplies the crossing from proposition to experienced consequence.
Painful punishment specifies the adverse effect that reaches the persisting speakers.
The pain-causing quality makes the threatened contact experiential rather than merely juridical.

changed_reading.before: A generic punishment is announced for a false belief.
changed_reading.after: A conditional interval remains in which the utterance can reach its end before its painful consequence reaches the persisting disbelievers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus demand to stop saying is surrounded by failures of learned authorities to prohibit sinful speech and of a community to prohibit one another from reprehensible action. Continued doctrine becomes a social inhibition failure, not only an individual's uncorrected opinion.

activation_trace.role: The doctrinal-saying image anchors the social mechanism to what the focus speakers continue to maintain.
Cessation is the focus ayah's required interruption of that maintained speech.
The failed act of restraining supplies institutional nonintervention as an enabling condition.
Sinful saying as a maintained position links the earlier leadership failure directly to speech.
Failure to restrain one another broadens the missing brake from leaders to reciprocal communal correction.
The reprehensible thing that should be repelled supplies the object and purpose of communal restraint.

structural_cues: 5:63 asks why religious authorities do not prohibit sinful saying.
5:79 repeats the reciprocal form: they did not prohibit one another from a reprehensible act.
5:73 places the same stopping root inside the consequence condition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated prohibition failures around saying and wrongdoing; I infer that nonintervention enables the focus doctrine to persist. A live alternative is that 5:63 and 5:79 address other misconduct and only analogically illuminate 5:73.

surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قَالُوا and يَقُولُونَ repeat the focus root around a compact counted formula.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, repetition among many may amplify a conceptually unsettled formula; social persistence can conceal instability rather than resolve it.

strongest_changes: The numerical correction became a rejection of dependent members and partition within deity.
The demand to desist became a communal inhibition problem as well as an individual decision.
The warning became reversible through the pericope's competing images of truth-covering and restorative covering.
The explicit reward because of what responsive hearers said made the focus saying part of a matched speech-to-consequence structure.
The focus's among them became a decisive subgroup restriction in light of later moderate and receptive trajectories.
summary.what_was_special: The pericope repeatedly converted a compact theological proposition into inspectable mechanisms: counted membership, embodied dependence, failed social restraint, competing coverings, matched returns for speech, and differentiated responses within a named population.
remaining_uncertainties: The indivisibility reading of one is branch-supported but may go beyond a narrower denial of partners.
The causal symmetry between the condemned saying and the rewarded saying may concern the dispositions voiced by speech rather than words independently.
The hearthstone, imposed-restraint, and split-root readings are live analogies but must remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Partitive counting is checked by peerless oneness.** `ث ل ث B002` is one third as a part, while `و ح د B003` is peerless uniqueness and `B004` God's exclusive oneness. I infer that the problem is not arithmetic complexity alone but treating the divine as a part within a divisible set.
2. **Unrestrained saying becomes bodily contact.** `ن ه ي B001` is restraint and `م س س B004` contact by an effect. Failure to stop speech leads to pain touching its speakers; I infer a movement from abstract formulation to embodied consequence.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Composed number is opposed to exclusive oneness.** Fixed **ث ل ث / B003** (“third or making a third”) and **B004** (“thing made of three parts”) structure the claim, while fixed **و ح د / B003** (“peerless uniqueness”) and **B004** (“God’s exclusive oneness”) deny peer-composition. 5:72 has already separated Lord and messenger in reported speech; 5:75–5:76 add bodily dependence and lack of independent disposal. I infer that a “third” presupposes a class of comparable units, whereas exclusive oneness blocks that operation. The rebuttal reads as a category correction, not a competing count within the same numerical set.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:75’s shared need to eat and 5:76’s negated disposal made exclusive oneness concrete rather than numerical only: the proposed comparable unit remained dependent.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi hareket ettirip sallandırma, nesnenin bulunduğu yerde kararlı duramaması ve hareketin çıkardığı sesi birlikte verir; bunlar tek bir fiziksel hareket olayının neden, sonuç ve işitsel yönleridir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak kolun hareket ettirme, sallanma, yerinde duramama ve hareket sesi anlamlarını kapsar; özel bir yapının anlamı genelleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi hareket ettirerek yerinden oynatmayı ve onun kararsızca sallanıp bulunduğu yerde duramamasını bildirir; bu hareketin çıkardığı ses de aynı olayın işitsel yönüdür.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eylem çekirdeğini türemiş eylem ve varlık adlarından ayırır; türemiş biçimlerin kapsamı yalın eylemin tamamına aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığa tapınma eylemini ve kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini anlatır. Türemiş kullanımlarda bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınma konusu sayılan varlıkları da adlandırır.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, tapınmayı anlamın temeli sayar; kişinin tapınmaya yönelmesini, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınılır kılma işlemini bu temelden türetir. Tapınma konusu sayılan yontular ve güneş örneği, varlık anlamının belirli uygulamalarıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı, bir kişinin kendi topluluğunda veya çağında benzeri bulunmamasını açıkça dalın çekirdeği yapar. Bu benzersizlik çoğunlukla üstünlük övgüsü taşır; belirli anlatımların yergide kullanılması da aynı benzeri olmama yapısına bağlı bir değer değişimidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Eşsizlik çekirdeği yalın nitelemede bulunur; topluluk, çağ, övgü ve yergi sınırları belirli yapılarda ayrıca korunmuştur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin belirli bir toplulukta veya çağda eşi ve benzeri bulunmamasıdır. Bu eşsizlik çoğu kullanımda üstünlük bildiren övgü, bazı yapılarda ise yergi taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir eylemi yasaklayıp engelleme ile kişinin yasaklanan şeyden geri durmasını ve insanların kötülükten birbirini alıkoymasını birlikte doğrular.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın yasaklama anlamını korur; vazgeçme, benliği tutma ve karşılıklı engelleme yalnızca kanıtlanan yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimseyi bir eylemden yasaklayarak, engelleyerek veya uyararak alıkoymak; ilgili yapılarda yasaklanan eylemden geri durmak ya da insanların birbirini kötülükten alıkoymasıdır.

facets.statement: Bir eylemin yapılmasını yasaklama, engelleme veya caydırma yoluyla durdurma.
Yasaklanan veya istenmeyen eylemden geri durma ve kendini tutma.
Bir topluluğun kötülük karşısında üyelerini karşılıklı olarak engellemesi.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıtlar, buyruğun karşıtı olan yasaklamayı, bir şeyi yaptırmamak için engellemeyi ve bunun sonucunda geri durmayı aynı çekirdek çevresinde birleştirir; karşılıklı engelleme bu çekirdeğin topluluk içindeki kullanımını gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: bir eylemi yasaklama, engelleme veya ondan geri durma

error_profile.preserves: Yasaklama, engelleme ve geri durma yönlerinin tümünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin başka bir kişiyi belirli bir eylemden men ettiği etkin kullanımda uygundur.

error_profile.loses: Kişinin kendiliğinden geri durmasını ve karşılıklı engellemeyi kapsamaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili ifade ağır acı verme ve cezalandırma çekirdeğini doğrular. Bunun dayaktan türediği ve sonra her ağır sıkıntıya aktarıldığı açıklaması ortak zorunlu anlam değil, bildirilen bir köken ve genişleme görüşüdür; dal ancak bu kayıtla kabul edilebilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım ad, eylem ve yok etmeye yönelik ceza yapısını ayırır; yapıya bağlı özel ceza bütün dala genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Birine ağır acı çektirme veya onu ağır biçimde cezalandırmadır. Dayak kökeni ve anlamın her türlü ağır sıkıntıya yayılması, çekirdeğin parçası değil aktarılan bir açıklamadır.

facets.statement: Bir kişiye ağır acı verilir veya ağır bir ceza uygulanır.
Belirli bir yapı, bütünüyle yok etmeye yönelik cezayı anlatır.
Bildirilen bir görüş anlamı dayaktan başlatır ve sonra her ağır sıkıntıya genişletir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek ağır acı verme ve cezalandırmadır; dayak kökeni ile her ağır sıkıntıya yayılma ise zorunlu anlamdan ayrı, aktarılan bir açıklamadır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Hem uygulanan ağır cezayı hem de birine şiddetli acı verme eylemini karşılayan çekirdek ifadedir.

error_profile.preserves: Ağır acı verme ile ceza uygulama bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Eyleyenin başka bir kişiye şiddetli acı verdiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Eyleyeni, etkileneni ve ağır acının verilmesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Cezanın hedefi bütünüyle ortadan kaldırmak olduğunda kullanılan özel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Cezalandırmayı ve yok etmeye yönelik özel sonucu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, bir şeyin veya kişinin acı verici olduğunu nitelemeyi de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: acı verme veya acı verici olma
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da başka bir kişide acı meydana getirme alanında doğrudan örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak ağır acı ve ceza eksenindedir; komşu ise şiddet veya ceza şartı olmadan acı verme eylemini ve acı verici niteliği kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak, acının bir başkasına uygulanmasını ve bunun ceza niteliği taşımasını içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, acıyı yaşayan kişinin bedensel veya ruhsal duyumunu merkez alır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Uygulanan ağır acı, etkilenen kişide acı duyumuna yol açar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak acının uygulanması ve cezalandırma yönündedir; komşu ise etkilenen kişinin acıyı hissetmesi durumudur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak, birine ağır acı veya ceza uygulanmasını çekirdek edinir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu, sınanma niteliğindeki sıkıntıların yanında rahatlığı ve mal ya da çocuklarla sınanmayı da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Ağır sıkıntı veya ceza, iki dalın kesiştiği deneyim alanıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odakta acı verme ve ceza vardır; komşuda belirleyici unsur iyi veya kötü bir durumun sınama işlevi görmesidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; acı verme, acı duyma ve sınanma adayları temel sınırları gösterdi, diğerleri belirli ceza türleri veya daha uzak şiddet sahneleridir.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه العذاب والعقوبة والإيجاع الشديد، والتعذيب، وما يذكره المصدر من أصل الضرب ثم استعارة كل شدة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: العذاب يقال منه عذب تعذيبا وناس يقولون أصل العذاب الضرب ثم استعير ذلك في كل شدة (maqayis)؛ عذبت الرجل وغيره تعذيبا والاسم العذاب (jamhara)؛ العذاب العقوبة وقد عذبته تعذيبا (sihah)؛ العذاب هو الإيجاع الشديد (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه طرف السوط واللسان، والخرقة أو السير المشدود، والخيط، والغصن، وأطراف السيور والشراك، وما كان من علاقة أو ذوابة متدلية.
يدخل فيه العذبة بمعنى القذاة في الماء، وكثرة القذى، وإزالة ما في الحوض من القذى أو عرمضه، مع شاهد تهذيب عن ماء لا رعي فيه ولا كلأ.
يدخل فيه وصف العذبي بمعنى الكريم الأخلاق.
يدخل فيه العذب الخارج على أثر الولد من الرحم، والعذابة بمعنى الرحم.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi açık biçimde geçişli acı verme fiilini ve acı veren nitelik bildiren sıfatları bir arada sunar. Bu çerçeve, acıyı hisseden özneyi değil acıyı oluşturan etkeni veya acı verici niteliği merkeze aldığı için birinci daldan ayrıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam çıplak daldır; tanım belirli bir kalıba bağlı değildir ve geçişli acı verme ile acı verici niteliği birlikte sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir etkenin başka birinde acı oluşturması veya bir kişinin, nesnenin ya da durumun acı verici nitelikte olmasıdır. Nitelik kullanımları, acıyı yaşayan tarafı değil acıya sebep olan tarafı tanımlar.

facets.statement: Temel işlem, acının başkasında meydana getirilmesi veya ona acı verilmesidir.
Sıfat kullanımları acı oluşturan ya da inciten niteliği bildirir.
Azap veya kişi için verilen örnekler, acı verici olma niteliğinin farklı taşıyıcılara uygulanabildiğini gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı geçişli acı verme ve acı verici nitelik etrafında birleştirir. Bir fiil başkasına acı vermeyi anlatır; sıfatlar ise azap, kişi veya benzeri bir taşıyıcının acı veren ya da inciten özellikte olduğunu belirtir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Geçişli işlem çekirdeğini en kısa biçimde verir ve acı verici sıfatların sebep tarafıyla bağlantısını korur.

error_profile.preserves: Başkasında acı oluşturma çekirdeğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Acı verici nitelik bildiren sıfat kullanımını tek başına tam olarak söylemez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Nitelik bildiren kullanımlarda kişi, şey veya durumun acı veren yanını doğal biçimde karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Acıya sebep olan niteliği korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Başkasına acı verme fiilinin daha doğal veya kişiler arası bağlamlarında kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Başkasına zarar verici etki yönünü korur.
error_profile.adds: Fiziksel acı dışındaki kırma ve üzme anlamlarını da çağırabilir.

error_profile.preserves: Bazı bağlamlarda acı verici sonuçla ilişkili olabilir.
error_profile.loses: Acı verme ve acı verici olma çekirdeğini genel olarak kapsamaz.
error_profile.collision: Azap ve ceza alanındaki komşu dallarla karışır.
